messages:
maya: Heads-up — prepping KMS integration plan for Redwood Private (customer VPC) control plane + data-plane. Need quick sanity check on BYOK vs. us-owned CMK, envelope rewrap strategy, audit logging expectations, and key rotation playbook. Anyone who did this recently?
jon: I did a similar integration for a banking customer last quarter. TL;DR: prefer customer-owned CMK (BYOK) when possible. Grants to our control-plane role for GenerateDataKey/Encrypt/Decrypt. Keeps audit & compliance in their account.
eli: Agree on BYOK for regulated customers. Implementation notes: use envelope encryption — per-tenant DEK (data key) generated via KMS GenerateDataKey, store DEK ciphertext with tenant metadata. Only control-plane has grant to decrypt. For data-plane transfers, use the DEK directly to avoid KMS on every tokenized op.
maya: For rotation: if customer rotates CMK, we need a rewrap flow to decrypt DEKs with old CMK and re-encrypt with new CMK (or call ReEncrypt). How do folks handle rate limits and large caches?
jon: Rewrap as a background rolling job. Throttle at worker-level, use SQS/dedicated queue per-tenant, and prioritize small tenants first. Also check KMS quota (Req/s) — request a service quota increase if onboarding many customers at once.
eli: Another option: use KMS ReEncrypt API so you don't expose plaintext to our workers: call ReEncrypt with SourceKeyId=old and DestinationKeyId=new. But note ReEncrypt still counts against KMS requests and requires both key permissions. Sample CLI: 
``` 
aws kms re-encrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://dek.cipher --destination-key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/NEW-KEY-ID
``` 
jon: And for grants: we create a grant that allows our control-plane role to GenerateDataKey/Decrypt for that CMK. Eg: 
``` 
aws kms create-grant --key-id alias/customer-cmk --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::REDWOOD-ACCOUNT:role/RedwoodControlPlaneRole --operations Encrypt Decrypt GenerateDataKey
``` 
maya: Audit logging — customers will want to see KMS usage in their CloudTrail. Recommend we require customers to enable management & data events for KMS and deliver logs to their own S3 + optionally to our SIEM via cross-account subscription. Also watch for RetireGrant/CreateGrant events.
sean: RBAC notes: no service account should be given raw CMK access. Use least privilege: a control-plane role scoped to kms:GenerateDataKey, kms:Decrypt on specific key ARNs only. Add a read-only "key-usage" mapping for tenant security contacts to view CloudTrail entries, not key policies.
kms-bot: system: grant created grantId=abc123 for arn:aws:iam::REDWOOD-ACCOUNT:role/RedwoodControlPlaneRole on key alias/customer-cmk (ops:Encrypt,Decrypt,GenerateDataKey)
eli: Edge cases: compromised key — runbook should include: 1) Revoke grants (kms:RevokeGrant), 2) Create new CMK / import new key material if BYOK, 3) ReEncrypt existing DEKs to new CMK (or generate new DEKs), 4) Rotate any cached DEKs in memory/storage, 5) Notify customer and kick IR timeline. Also capture CloudTrail evidence before any rewraps.
maya: Good. I'll draft RFC + checklist: onboarding steps (policy template, grant creation, CloudTrail config, rewrap job), incident runbook, and a small terraform module for grant + alias + policy. Tagging @jon @eli @sean for review. :thumbsup:
jon: +1. Add a small test harness that simulates forced key rotation and validates rewrap success and fallback to cached DEKs.
eli: I'll add the CloudTrail detection rules to our SIEM playbook and include a query to detect unusual RetireGrant events.
maya: Thanks team — capturing notes and will drop RFC in #eng-security-rfcs later.
